age.evidence: All C57Bl6/J mice (male; 6-8 weeks old; The Jackson Laboratory)

dosing.evidence: Psilocybin powder ... was diluted in 0.9% sterile saline ... and administered intraperitonally (IP) at doses between 0.3 - 3 mg/kg.

handling.evidence: acclimated to University of Wisconsin vivarium conditions for at least seven-days prior to handling or experimentation

group_housing.evidence: housed in groups of three or four

assays.assay_description: Automated magnetometer-based detection of head twitches in an acrylic cylinder (15.24 × 15.24 cm); 1 h baseline pre-injection and 4 h post-injection recording; 10 min bins analyzed.

setup_restrain.evidence: connected to a flexible tether (ZC16) to record EEG while allowing free range of motion

food_restriction.evidence: No food present in recording cylinder

water_restriction.evidence: No water present in recording cylinder

time_to_assay.evidence: the animals were administered 3 mg/kg IP psilocybin and recorded for an additional 4 h

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (3 mg/kg, i.p.) significantly increased head-twitch counts in the first 10 min after injection compared to saline or ketamine, returning to baseline within 2 h.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way RM ANOVA, Finteraction(36,360)=3.97, p<0.0001; Tukey's q(7.17)=6.92, p=0.0041 vs saline; q(6.36)=7.33, p=0.0042 vs ketamine.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin-treated animals demonstrated a clear elevation in the number of head-twitch responses occurring in the 10 min after IP administration as compared to saline or ketamine.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Time course of automated head twitch response detections across each 10 min time period

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is explicitly excluded by rubric

B7_automated_classification.evidence: magnetometer signal processed in MATLAB; not pose estimation or ML video classifier

E1_environment_type.evidence: clear acrylic cylinder (15.24 cm height x 15.24 cm diameter)

E7_social_context.evidence: individual animals were placed into a clear acrylic cylinder

D1_continuity.evidence: Continuous recording 1 h pre + 4 h post = single session

D2_session_duration.evidence: recorded for 1 h prior to drug administration ... administered 3 mg/kg IP psilocybin and recorded for an additional 4 h

D4_baseline.evidence: recorded ... for 1 h prior to drug administration

D5_followup.evidence: recording ends within 4 h of injection

assays.assay_description: 41 × 20 × 24 cm arena with center zone defined as middle one-third (6 × 27 cm); 10 min sessions in acute experiments and 150 min sessions in long-term experiments; assessed at 5–15 min, 4 h, and 7 days post-injection. Outcomes: total distance and time in center, tracked with Any-Maze.

application_type.evidence: Mice were injected IP with psilocybin (0 - 3 mg/kg)

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were allowed to explore freely for 10 minutes ... and 150 min in long-term experiments

food_restriction.evidence: no food in OFT arena during testing

water_restriction.evidence: no water in OFT arena during testing

time_to_assay.evidence: at a time period from 5 min to 7 days afterward (acute 5–15 min; post-acute 4 h; long-term 7 days)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin dose-dependently increased locomotor distance acutely (15 min); high doses acutely decreased time in center (anxiogenic) while at 4 h higher doses increased center time (anxiolytic). One week after psilocybin alone, center time was increased; chronic corticosterone exposure reversed this to an anxiogenic-like decrease. Brief isoflurane post-injection abolished the long-term effect.
outcomes.statistics: Distance 15 min: F(3,40)=4.62, p=0.0073; linear trend F(1,40)=13.39, p=0.0007; Tukey 3 mg/kg vs saline q(40)=5.13, p=0.0042. Center 15 min: F(2,27), p=0.0137; linear trend F(1,27)=10.08, p=0.0037. Center 4 h: F(2,26)=3.37, p=0.0498; linear trend F(1,26)=6.72, p=0.0155. Correlation 15 min vs 4 h: R²=-0.95, p=0.0264. Long-term OFT interaction Finteraction(1,28)=5.95, p=0.0213; Sidak t(28)=3.605, p=0.0072. Isoflurane-no-CORT t(14)=2.607, p=0.0207.
outcomes.evidence: low-dose (0.3 mg/kg) psilocybin increased the time in center ... higher doses exhibited a dose-dependent reduction ... at 4 h after treatment, low-dose psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) decreased the time in center, while higher doses exhibited a dose-dependent increase.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Time spent in the center and total distance travelled were automatically quantified

B4_ethological.evidence: locomotor distance and zone time only

E6_spatial.evidence: open field with virtual center zone

D1_continuity.evidence: OFT recorded at 15 min, 4 h, and 7 days across experiments

D3_recording_days.evidence: tested at 5 min, 4 h, and 7 days afterward

assays.assay_description: 46 × 10 cm clear Plexiglas swim tank with 26 °C water; 6 min test, immobility and distance scored for final 4 min using Any-Maze; tested at 4 h post-injection.

application_type.evidence: Mice were injected IP with either psilocybin (3 mg/kg)

setup_restrain.evidence: individually placed into a clear Plexiglas swim tank (46x10cm) for 6 min (FST is rubric-defined restraint)

water_restriction.evidence: no drinkable water in swim tank

sample_size.evidence: F(2,31) for ketamine analysis implies ~34 total across groups

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (3 mg/kg) did not change immobility time in the FST at 4 h post-injection, while ketamine produced a robust reduction.
outcomes.statistics: Ketamine vs saline/psilocybin: F(2,31)=30.56, p<0.0001; Sidaks t(31)=7.03, p<0.0001 (ket vs saline); t(31)=6.36, p<0.0001 (ket vs psilo).
outcomes.evidence: no psilocybin-induced changes in behavioral despair were observed, using immobility time in the FST (Figure 1B).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Immobility time and distance travelled were quantified

D3_recording_days.evidence: tested at 4 h post-injection on one day

assays.assay_description: Individual cages with two-bottle choice (1% sucrose vs water) after 48 h habituation and three 16 h restriction cycles; consumption measured periodically over up to 15 days post-injection.

setup_habituation.evidence: mice were placed into individual housing (41x20x24cm) to habituate for 48 h

food_restriction.evidence: mice had ad libitum access to standard chow and the 2 bottles provided

water_restriction.evidence: Animals underwent three 16 h restriction periods during which they had access to the 1% sucrose solution and water

time_to_assay.evidence: measurements 0–24 h after drug administration and across 1–7 days/up to 15 days

sample_size.evidence: n=7-8 per group for chronic conditions; ANOVA F(3,27)=7.49

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin had no significant effect on sucrose preference post-acutely (0–12 h) nor long-term (1–7 days). The only notable acute effect was that psilocybin masked the avoidance of corticosterone-containing water in CORT-exposed animals.
outcomes.statistics: ANOVA F(3,27)=7.49, p=0.0008; Sidak saline vs saline+CORT t(27)=3.441, p=0.0057.
outcomes.evidence: There was also no significant effect of psilocybin on hedonic responding, as measured by the sucrose preference post-acutely (Figure 1C). No long-term effects of psilocybin or ketamine on sucrose preference were observed.

B4_ethological.evidence: preference score is not an ethological behaviour

E1_environment_type.evidence: mice were placed into individual housing (41x20x24cm) ... two identical bottles ... placed into each cage

E2_shelter.evidence: no shelter described in test cage

E8_food_water.evidence: mice had ad libitum access to standard chow and the 2 bottles provided

D1_continuity.evidence: measurements taken across multiple periods (0–24 h, 1, 3, 5, 7 days, up to 15 days)

D2_session_duration.evidence: Three 16 h restriction periods ... consumption measured for a period of up to 15 days

D3_recording_days.evidence: consumption was measured for a period of up to 15 days

D5_followup.evidence: Sucrose preference for 1-7 days in drug-treated animals

assays.assay_description: Brightly illuminated novel cage (61 × 41 × 37 cm) with a 50% sucrose-soaked food pellet in a central petri dish; animals fasted 16–24 h; latency to first feed scored by blinded observer over 10 min; movement tracked with Any-Maze.

application_type.evidence: Mice then received an IP injection of saline or drug 4-5 h prior to performing the NSF test

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were then placed into a corner of the apparatus and allowed to explore for 10 minutes

food_restriction.evidence: Animals underwent a sequential food reduction of 2-Days at 20% and 1-day at 80% and food deprivation (16 - 24 h)

time_to_assay.evidence: an IP injection of saline or drug 4-5 h prior to performing the NSF test

sample_size.evidence: n = 20 across treatment in survival analysis; t(18)=2.25

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (3 mg/kg) reduced latency to feed at 4 h post-injection, indicating post-acute anxiolysis. This effect was lost in animals chronically exposed to oral corticosterone. No effect of ketamine.
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin treatment did demonstrate post-acute anxiolytic-like effects through reduction in the latency to first consumption in the NSF at 4 h post-treatment (Figure 1D; Student's t-test; t(18) = 2.25; p = 0.0372).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Latency to first feed ... movement and distance traveled ... Pellet weights were also obtained immediately before and after each test

B4_ethological.evidence: Feeding (consumption of food pellet) is a natural ethological behaviour scored

B7_automated_classification.evidence: latency scored by blinded observer; Any-Maze used for tracking only

E1_environment_type.evidence: novel cage environment (61x41x37cm) that was brightly illuminated

E7_social_context.evidence: Mice were then placed into a corner of the apparatus

E8_food_water.evidence: a food pellet soaked in 50% sucrose solution was placed into a glass petri dish that served as the feeding zone

judge_notes: Merged candidates' separate OFT entries (acute 5–15 min, 4 h, 7-day, with/without isoflurane, with/without CORT) into one Open Field Test assay per rubric (same apparatus and outcomes, different drug/timepoint/manipulation conditions).
Merged longitudinal SPT measurements (0–24 h and 1–15 days) into one Sucrose Preference Test assay (multiple recording days of the same paradigm).
B4 ethological scored 1 for NSF because actual feeding/consumption is a natural ethological behaviour; HTR, FST immobility, OFT zone time, and sucrose preference do not qualify per rubric.
B7 scored 0 throughout: Any-Maze is position-tracking and HTR detection is magnetometer signal processing in MATLAB, neither qualifies as a behavioural classifier under the rubric.
FST coded as setup_restrain = yes per rubric (FST cylinder is listed as restraint).

SPT environment categorized as 'Home cage' (E1=1) because testing occurred in the animals' individual housing cage with food/water continuously available; E8 scored Yes; D2 set to 16 h restriction window (61 min–6 h) and D6 scored Yes given individual sessions span >6 h.
n values and some housing details (handling, day_night_flipped, enrichment) marked not_reported with low confidence as the paper is silent.
